summary: deploy.sh: self-heal ownership before prune; tolerate root-owned releases left by emergency manual sudo runs
description:
Old release dirs in /srv/guru-web/releases/ accumulated root-owned files from earlier emergency 'sudo /srv/guru-web/deploy.sh' runs (before we standardised on 'sudo -u deploy'). The CI prune step ('xargs -r -I{} rm -rf -- {}') silently fails on those, so old releases pile up forever and the disk fills.

Fix:
- deploy.sh runs 'sudo chown -R deploy:deploy /srv/guru-web/releases' at the top (idempotent, '|| true' so the deploy proceeds even if sudoers isn't updated yet on the VPS).
- vps-bootstrap.sh adds the corresponding NOPASSWD sudoers line.
- deploy/README.md adds an operator note about updating /etc/sudoers.d/deploy on existing VPSes (one-time hand patch — bootstrap already ran).

Done when:
- Self-heal line present in deploy.sh, before the prune.
- vps-bootstrap.sh's sudoers heredoc includes the chown rule.
- README documents the one-time sudoers patch operators must apply on existing VPSes.
- Test asserts deploy.sh contains the self-heal command (source-level).

resolution.note: Self-heal chown at top of deploy.sh, gated by '|| true' for safe rollout. New sudoers rule in vps-bootstrap.sh; existing VPSes need a one-time hand-patch documented in deploy/README.md.
